A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PuzzleMoE and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Their methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting, renumbering and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on four MoE models, downstream accuracy, perplexity, inference measurements, ablations and results across 16 expert-grouping seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds HumanEval evaluation, kernel benchmarks, throughput sweeps, weight-distribution analyses and expanded sparsity and saliency experiments.

M1.justification: v1 describes a custom CUDA GEMV kernel; v2 introduces a fused Triton decode-GEMM kernel that concatenates paired experts' inputs and accesses their packed weight tensor once to compute both outputs (Section 3.3.2, Figure 5). This substantially changes inference execution, while the dual-mask merging equations and bit-packing format remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds HumanEval code generation on Qwen1.5-MoE (Appendix A.7, Table 8), a focused extension into coding. WikiText-2, the seven general benchmarks, GSM8K, Math-500 and AIME24/25 are retained; the mathematical reasoning evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds D2 to the Qwen1.5 and Qwen3 comparisons and HC-SMoE+AWQ to the quantization comparisons. New kernel benchmarks compare against cuBLAS. Conversely, the end-to-end efficiency comparison drops Wanda, NAEE and HC-SMoE, comparing only the full model with PuzzleMoE. Comparator coverage therefore changes substantially across accuracy, quantization and systems experiments.

E3.justification: The reported systems evaluation changes from A100 deployments with 1024/512 prefill/decode lengths to an eight-RTX5090 cluster with batch and sequence-length sweeps. New microbenchmarks vary matrix dimensions on RTX4090/5090. v2 also evaluates 37.5%, 66.7% and 75% sparsity and introduces HumanEval Pass@1. The existing C4 calibration size, sequence length and similarity threshold are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds Gaussian weight-distribution checks, router-aware saliency ablations, higher-sparsity robustness tests and kernel/workload scaling analyses (Appendices A.1, A.2, A.5 and A.8). Existing calibration, grouping, threshold and merge-group-size analyses remain; several are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 16 random expert-grouping seeds and report means and standard deviations. The numerical contents of v1 Tables 11–14 and v2 Tables 13–16 match exactly. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: HC-SMoE's Qwen3 average accuracy changes from 54.9/37.2 to 62.4/54.9 at 25%/50% sparsity (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 1), while PuzzleMoE's corresponding results remain unchanged. Added results include HumanEval Pass@1 of 45.1/39.6, higher-sparsity scores and kernel benchmarks. Compression timings also change, and earlier memory/speed results are replaced. The new 1.80× throughput maximum uses different settings from v1's 1.28× result.

T1.justification: The Gaussian similarity-probability derivation is retained from v1 Appendix B.2 in v2 Appendix A.6. However, the new informal Lemma 3.1 states the variance-independent formula without the near-equal-variance qualification attached to that simplification in both appendices. This introduces a limited discrepancy in the stated assumptions.

C1.justification: The central claims about fine-grained dual-mask merging and metadata-free bit-packing remain. The abstract and contribution list replace the 1.28× inference-speed claim with up to 1.80× end-to-end throughput, change the stated benchmark count from seven to nine, and drop the headline 45× compression-time claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting throughput gains to shared weight access and their attenuation to uncompressed attention, and interprets router-aware ablations as showing little additional benefit from gating signals. It distinguishes the packing scheme's pairwise restriction from higher-sparsity merging with explicit metadata. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit conclusion warning about the roughly ten-point AIME25 accuracy loss.

D1.justification: v2 specifies Triton implementation and profiling, RTX5090/4090 hardware, benchmark matrix dimensions and batch configurations, and explicitly identifies Qwen3's reasoning mode. These refine implementation and evaluation documentation. The code-access link and established calibration, threshold and quantization details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the dense-model-merging subsection and its Localize-and-Stitch, LoRS-Merging and model-merging-survey references, while adding HumanEval and QLoRA citations. The principal positioning against expert dropping and coarse-grained expert merging remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. A new motivation subsection brings existing appendix reasoning into the main text, selected ablations move to an expanded appendix, and an impact statement replaces neither the removed LLM-usage statement nor its purpose. The title changes from sparse to fine-grained expert merging.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 redraws the merging diagram, adds a fused-kernel diagram, kernel and throughput plots, and weight-distribution histograms, and expands comparison tables. The original memory/speed panels disappear; existing similarity plots and several tables are relocated or redisplayed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central inference contribution through cuBLAS comparisons on two GPU types and batch/sequence sweeps, addressing v1's limited isolation of kernel benefits. Coding evaluations, broader comparisons and expanded ablations also clarify applicability. These gains outweigh losing the earlier competitor memory/speed comparisons and explicit AIME25 limitation, although the new lemma's missing variance qualification reduces mathematical precision. The improvement rests on stronger validation, not a direct comparison of the differently measured speedup maxima.
